CVT Control (Computer)
A transmission control computer integrated with the engine control computer has been adopted. Various signals are communicated between the engine and transmission control computers to perform integrated engine control, achieving both smooth shift characteristics and excellent shift response at a high level.
Acceleration control (linear feel improvement control), NAVI AI-SHIFT and uphill/downhill shift control have been adopted to achieve smooth shift characteristics and excellent shift response, and neutral control has been adopted to improve fuel economy while the vehicle is stopped.
Diagnosis and fail-safe functions are provided for serviceability in the event of a system malfunction.

Components and Functions
Components Function
Shift Control Duty Solenoid No.1 (DS1) Controls the inflow of line pressure to the primary pulley according to the wheel speed and accelerator opening. (Controls the speed of upshifting)
Shift Control Duty Solenoid No.2 (DS2) Controls the line pressure and outflow from the primary pulley according to the wheel speed and accelerator opening. (Controls the speed of downshifting)
Lock-up Solenoid (SL) Switches the function of the linear solenoid (SLS).
Lock-up Engagement Pressure Control Duty Solenoid (DSU) Controls the gradual increase and decrease of the lock-up engagement hydraulic pressure.
Belt Clamping Force Control Linear Solenoid (SLS) Controls the secondary pulley pressure according to the input shaft torque to control the belt clamping force. In addition, it controls the forward/reverse clutch hydraulic pressure during forward/reverse clutch engagement and during neutral control.
Primary Pulley Speed Sensor (NIN) Detects the input shaft speed.
Secondary Pulley Speed Sensor (N0UT) Detects the output shaft speed.
Turbine Speed Sensor (NT) Detects the turbine speed.
Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Detects the belt clamping force.
Fluid Temperature Sensor Detects the fluid temperature.
Water Temperature Sensor Detects the engine coolant temperature.
Accelerator Position Sensor Detects the accelerator opening.
Throttle Position Sensor Detects the throttle valve opening angle.
Crankshaft Position Sensor Detects the engine speed.
Stop Light Switch Detects the ON/OFF state of the brake pedal.
Neutral Start Switch Detects the shift position of the automatic transaxle.
G Sensor Detects the inclination angle of the vehicle.
Shift Position Indicator (Built into Combination Meter) Informs the driver of the shift position in use through the LCD display.
Sport Sequential Shiftmatic Switch Detects whether sport sequential mode is selected.
Engine Control Computer (Integrated with Transmission Control Computer) Performs integrated control of the engine and transaxle and transaxle control based on the signals from each sensor. A diagnosis mode and fail-safe functions are provided for serviceability in the event of a system malfunction.
